correctness.rationale: Matrix–Tree yields T=z E_(a-1)(u) E_(b-1)(v)+E_(a-1)(u) product(v)+product(u) E_(b-1)(v) for independently variable edges. Because the graph is simple, the conductance-to-reduced-Laplacian map is injective; log det is strictly concave over positive-definite reduced Laplacians, giving unique optimum with positive determinant. The polynomial is invariant under independent within-route permutations, so uniqueness forces equal route conductances x,y despite no graph automorphism assumption. For T=x^(a-1)y^(b-1)(a*y+b*x+ab*z), Euler and KKT give the rational interior solution and the unique decreasing root of G(r)=1/r-(a-1)/(a^2p-r)-(b-1)/(b^2q-r). The shortcut-free positive quadratic for x/y and its KKT directional derivative give sharp support at all r; envelope identity yields quadratic contact. Independently computed a=2,b=3 reduced-Laplacian determinants and exact optima for r=1 and boundary r=3/2; these finite checks support the all-length proof.

final_claim: For a two-terminal theta graph with long routes of lengths a,b>=2 and one direct shortcut, with independently adjustable edge conductances priced p,q within routes and shortcut price r, a fixed budget B has a unique spanning-tree-determinant maximizing design. The shortcut is present exactly for r below an explicit quadratic threshold r_c, equal to ab*s/(a+b-1) when p=q=s; near the threshold its optimal weight vanishes linearly and logarithmic determinant advantage quadratically.
